supercharger_access.notes: Quick web lookup. Source says every Model Y uses a native NACS port; Supercharger access follows from that.

consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, temperature not stated, 20-30 mph winds, wheel size not stated, battery-side (car display, Out of Spec Reviews method; page does not say explicitly) | Out of Spec Reviews, 2025 Model Y Long Range AWD (Juniper), 298 miles. Page says 'around 3.7 miles per kWh': one rounded figure given for both the old and new Long Range AWD together, and the page does not state the pack: 1000 / (3.7 x 1.609344) = 168 Wh/km. Other figures seen, not recorded: tparts.com relays 275 Wh/mi (171 Wh/km) for the same test; Bjorn Nyland Juniper Premium AWD 20.1 kWh/100 km at 120 km/h but only 12 C (autonomiacocheselectricos.es, no video link); AutoReview.nl LR AWD 20.04 kWh/100 km at 130 km/h, 19 C, 14.75 kWh/100 km at 100 km/h.

heat_pump.notes: Quick web lookup. 2027 US-oriented page says the Model Y heat pump is standard; 2026 Canadian model assumed the same.
Estimated: EV Database lists heat pump as standard equipment on the Model Y Premium AWD (Juniper, Berlin); same model and generation carries it over. Not confirmed for this exact variant.
